BinkMovie/BINKMovie.cpp.classification: platform replacement with restored original subtitle route
BinkMovie/BINKMovie.cpp.reason: The FFmpeg consumer keeps int-sized enums and now preserves subtitle arguments through a separately compiled engine-ABI adapter. The original subtitle owners are selected; opaque handles, font pointers and uint32_t ticks preserve the enum seam. Captions follow uploaded-frame PTS, and original font/render ownership ends through movie cleanup. Actual-owner mixed-enum sanitizer fixtures exercise production Bink lifecycle bodies with simulated decoder/GPU APIs.

Complete native link/package identity and retail visual, glyph, subtitle-coverage and A/V timing acceptance remain separate gates under the play-test hold. PTS-based 60-Hz timing intentionally differs from the released SDK's one-based frame-count and integer frame-rate arithmetic.

BinkMovie/subtitle.cpp.reason: The original caption owner is staged and selected with engine enum/wchar ABI. Explicit UTF-16 copy/length operations replace incompatible libc wchar calls while retaining authored defaults and caption ownership.
BinkMovie/subtitle.cpp.remaining: Full-link retention and retail glyph/presentation acceptance remain independent gates; see reports/MOVIE_SUBTITLE_RESTORATION.md.

BinkMovie/subtitleparser.cpp.classification: restored original engine owner with portability hardening
BinkMovie/subtitleparser.cpp.reason: The original parser is staged and selected. Fifty-four original-parser checks and the mixed-enum owner fixtures pass under ASan/UBSan.
BinkMovie/subtitleparser.cpp.remaining: Audit complete retail subtitle format/coverage and native presentation; synthetic non-play fixtures do not establish content parity.

Tests execute original owners and font reference methods across short-enum/int-enum translation units.
BinkMovie/subtitlemanager.cpp.remaining: Native symbol retention, retail caption placement and timing remain independent evidence gates; see reports/MOVIE_SUBTITLE_RESTORATION.md.
